item.title: Which pollen is found in honey? Automated analysis closely matches conventional testing
item.description: Pure rapeseed honey—or not quite? Single-flower honeys must contain a certain proportion of pollen from the respective plant. This is assessed by pollen analysis, which is time-consuming and requires specialist expertise. As part of a collaborative project, a research team from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ) and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv) in Leipzig worked with several partners to develop an automated, AI-based pollen analysis method for honey testing. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The Guardian view on Cop31: a just transition needs more than fine words | Editorial
item.description: Petrostates blocked ambition while wealthy nations withheld cash support. The climate crisis demands the next UN summit turns promises into action In a negotiation the maxim is usually that no deal is better than a bad deal. But the failure of Cop31 in Turkey to get a climate pact – the first time this has happened in 17 years – should not be an excuse for leaving the planet with the damaging status quo. A hard bargain needs a credible route to agreement: by making commitments, seeking concessions and getting others to reciprocate. This did not happen at the weekend. item.title: Engineering study reshapes understanding of remotely triggered earthquakes
item.description: Understanding earthquake mechanisms and mitigating earthquake hazards remain a critical global challenge. For decades, seismologists have observed that seismic waves of large earthquakes can trigger seismic activity at distances of thousands of kilometers—a phenomenon known as remote (dynamic) triggering. Yet two puzzles persisted: Why do some triggered events occur long after the seismic waves have passed? And why do Rayleigh waves, which carry lower shear stresses than Love waves, appear more effective at triggering? Fuente: Phys.org.
